ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertices $A$ and $B$ of the isosceles $\triangle ABC$ are located on the $x$-axis and $y$-axis, respectively. The graph of the inverse proportion function $y= \frac{k}{x}$ ($k>0$, $x>0$) passes through the right-angle vertex $C$. If $OA=7$ and $OB=3$, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, construct $CE\perp y$-axis, $CD\perp x$-axis. Since $\angle O=90^\circ$, it follows that quadrilateral $ODCE$ is a rectangle. Therefore, $\angle ECD=90^\circ$. Since $\angle BCA=90^\circ$, it follows that $\angle ECB=\angle DCA$. Therefore, in $\triangle CEB$ and $\triangle CDA$, we have $\left\{\begin{array}{l} \angle CEB=\angle CDA \\ \angle ECB=\angle DCA \\ CB=CA \end{array}\right.$ Therefore, $\triangle CEB\cong \triangle CDA\left(AAS\right)$, which implies $CE=CD$, $EB=DA$. Consequently, quadrilateral $ODCE$ is a square. Let $EB=DA=x$, so $OD=OA-DA=7-x$, $OE=OB+BE=3+x$. Since $OE=OD$, we get $7-x=3+x$, which is solved to find $x=2$. Therefore, $OD=7-2=5$, $OE=3+2=5$. Hence, the coordinates of point C are $(5,5)$. Substituting $C(5,5)$ into $y=\frac{k}{x}$ gives $5=\frac{k}{5}$. Solving this yields $k=\boxed{25}$.

method.method_draft: Use an auxiliary-rectangle congruence argument. From the image, read that A is on the positive x-axis, B is on the positive y-axis, C is in the first quadrant above/right of both axes, and the right-isosceles triangle ABC has its right angle at C. From the text, use OA=7, OB=3, AC=BC, and the hyperbola y=k/x through C. Drop perpendiculars from C to the axes: CD perpendicular to the x-axis with D on OA, and CE perpendicular to the y-axis with E above B. Then ODCE is a rectangle. Since angle BCA is 90 degrees and angle ECD is also 90 degrees, the acute angle between CE and CB equals the acute angle between CD and CA. With right angles at E and D and hypotenuses CB=CA, triangles CEB and CDA are congruent, so CE=CD and EB=DA. Thus ODCE is actually a square. Let EB=DA=t. Then OD=OA-DA=7-t and OE=OB+EB=3+t. Since OD=OE, solve 7-t=3+t to get t=2, so C=(OD,OE)=(5,5). Finally, because C lies on y=k/x, compute k=xy=5·5=25.

method.method_draft: Use coordinate/vector equations for a right isosceles triangle. From the image, take O as the origin, A on the positive x-axis and B on the positive y-axis, with C in the first quadrant on the hyperbola. From the text, assign A=(7,0), B=(0,3), and let C=(u,v) with u>0, v>0. Since C is the right-angle vertex, vectors A-C=(7-u,-v) and B-C=(-u,3-v) are perpendicular, giving (7-u)(-u)+(-v)(3-v)=0, i.e. u^2+v^2-7u-3v=0. raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the vertices $A$ and $B$ of the isosceles $\triangle ABC$ are located on the $x$-axis and $y$-axis, respectively. The graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{k}{x}$ ($k>0$, $x>0$) passes through the right-angle vertex $C$. If $OA=7$ and $OB=3$, what is the value of $k$?
raw_record.answer: Solution: As shown in the figure, construct $CE\perp y$-axis, $CD\perp x$-axis. Since $\angle O=90^\circ$, it follows that quadrilateral $ODCE$ is a rectangle. Therefore, $\angle ECD=90^\circ$. Since $\angle BCA=90^\circ$, it follows that $\angle ECB=\angle DCA$. Therefore, in $\triangle CEB$ and $\triangle CDA$, we have $\left\{\begin{array}{l} \angle CEB=\angle CDA \\ \angle ECB=\angle DCA \\ CB=CA \end{array}\right.$ Therefore, $\triangle CEB\cong \triangle CDA\left(AAS\right)$, which implies $CE=CD$, $EB=DA$. Consequently, quadrilateral $ODCE$ is a square. Let $EB=DA=x$, so $OD=OA-DA=7-x$, $OE=OB+BE=3+x$. Since $OE=OD$, we get $7-x=3+x$, which is solved to find $x=2$. Therefore, $OD=7-2=5$, $OE=3+2=5$. Hence, the coordinates of point $C$ are $(5,5)$. Substituting $C(5,5)$ into $y=\frac{k}{x}$ gives $5=\frac{k}{5}$. Solving this yields $k=\boxed{25}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin, A is on the positive x-axis, and B is on the positive y-axis; the line segments BA, BC, and CA form triangle ABC, point C is located in the first quadrant, and an inverse proportional function curve passes through C. In the figure, C is above A and to the upper right of B, consistent with the situation of drawing perpendiculars from C to the x-axis and y-axis to construct an auxiliary rectangle.

Then reason: According to the problem, △ABC is an isosceles right triangle with C as the right-angle vertex, so ∠BCA=90° and CA=CB. Draw CD⊥x-axis through C, with foot D; draw CE⊥y-axis, with foot E. Because the coordinate axes are perpendicular to each other, quadrilateral ODCE is a rectangle, so ∠ECD=90°. Also ∠BCA=90°, and a common included angle can be correspondingly decomposed from the two angles, so ∠ECB=∠DCA. In △CEB and △CDA, ∠CEB=∠CDA=90°, ∠ECB=∠DCA, and CB=CA, therefore △CEB≅△CDA, obtaining CE=CD, EB=DA. Thus adjacent sides of rectangle ODCE are equal, so it is a square, hence OD=OE.

Let EB=DA=t. Given OA=7, OB=3, then OD=OA-DA=7-t, OE=OB+EB=3+t. Because OD=OE, 7-t=3+t, solving gives t=2. Thus OD=5, OE=5, so the coordinates of C are (5,5). The inverse proportional function y=k/x passes through C, therefore k=xy=5×5=25.
